summary: AI equities are trading at 10-20 year low valuation multiples, implying market consensus of peak spending
summary_extended: Baker argues that AI-related equities are broadly trading at 10-15, and in some cases 20-year low valuation multiples, which he interprets as the stock market pricing in a consensus view that AI capex spending has peaked. He views this as a potentially significant mispricing if AI continues to grow more economically useful and capital deployment into infrastructure remains elevated or accelerates. The investment implication is that AI equities broadly — spanning infrastructure, semiconductors, and software — may represent a contrarian long opportunity, as the market appears to be discounting a peak-spending scenario that Baker does not believe is inevitable. He frames this valuation observation as the central question he is actively pressing management teams on, suggesting it is a live, high-conviction portfolio-level thesis rather than a speculative observation. No specific company names or numerical capex figures were cited in this segment, making this a macro-level sector thesis rather than a single-stock call.
